gist: Gloucester and holders Bordeaux Begles drew 36-36 in a thrilling Champions Cup match.
Both teams scored five tries each during the see-saw Pool Three encounter.
A moment of silence was held before kick-off for Lions lock Hyron Andrews.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Gloucester and title holders Bordeaux Begles played out a 36-36 draw at Kingsholm in their Champions Cup opener. The visitors led early through Martin Page-Relo, but Gloucester responded with tries from Arthur Clark, Max Llewellyn and George Barton to lead 24-17 at half-time. Bordeaux hit back through Sipili Falatea, Pablo Uberti and Louis Bielle-Biarrey. Gloucester replacement Will Trenholm scored twice midway through the second half, before Bielle-Biarrey's second try and Maxime Lucu's conversion levelled the match. Neither side could secure a late winner.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Bordeaux, aiming to win the tournament for a third consecutive year, avoided what would have been their first defeat in the competition since April 2024. Before kick-off, players observed a moment's silence following the death of Lions lock Hyron Andrews on Friday at the age of 31.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Lions will play their scheduled fixture against La Rochelle on Saturday in honour of Andrews, with further tributes planned across the opening round of the Champions Cup.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: After a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, defender Lisandro Martinez publicly criticised Manchester United's hierarchy for insufficient investment in the squad. He specifically questioned the technical director, Jason Wilcox, and suggested the club failed to build a strong enough team following their Champions League qualification. The club has struggled recently, failing to win in five matches.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The comments have sparked debate regarding player conduct and club management. Former players Wayne Rooney and Ashley Young argued the public criticism was disrespectful to teammates and could harm dressing room morale. Conversely, some observers and fans feel Martinez's honesty reflects long-standing concerns about recruitment and ownership decisions under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Omar Berrada.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Manager Michael Carrick, who has not yet seen the full interview, indicated he would address the matter after gathering more information. The club faces ongoing pressure regarding its recruitment strategy, financial debt, and the performance of the current squad.
